calls.reason: OpenAI's GPT-4 notes back the unreliability point, but the only controlled study (Cohn et al. 2024) found that anthropomorphic cues had no effect on overall trust. The causal link to hype and overtrust remains unshown.

The MIT/Nature MI study found that users' mental models matter more with GPT-3 than with ELIZA. That points to a possible mechanism, but it measured perceptions rather than harmful reliance, and nothing establishes the historical increase.

The only evidence is a research agent architecture with a memory stream, not the GPT-4 or Bard products. No retention test of those products was obtained, and the 'inner agent' clause has no workable test.

OpenAI's own GPT-4 notes support the fabrication point, and the ABC's Replika interviews show attachment and distress. But the harm pathways are hedged with 'can', and nothing ties them to attributing intelligence to the bots.
